newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPO - Tirupati Luke Ltd.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPO - Tirupati Luke Ltd.

text.p: The following initial public issue (IPO) by India's Tirupati Luke Ltd is expected to be open for public subscription on November 15:

Tirupati Luke is seeking public funds to finance an export- oriented floriculture unit. The project with a facility to cultivate 3.12 million roses and cut flowers is estimated to cost 55 million rupees.

The project cost of 55 million rupees is to be financed through equity -- 20 million rupees from promoters and 35 million rupees from the public. Project cost includes 11 million rupees for land and building, 9.80 million rupees for imported rose plants, 12 million rupees for greenhouse, three million rupees for irrigation systems, two million rupees for miscellaneous assets, four million rupees for vehicles, four million rupees as technology fees, 3.40 million rupees for cold storage facilities, 2.40 million rupees for public issue expenses and 3.40 million rupees for pre-operative expenses and contingencies.

The company propose to bring five acres of land under a greenhouse to cultivate cut flowers with maximum capacity of 3.12 million flowers per annum. After three years of operation the company proposes to double capacity to 6.24 million flowers.
The land located at Salgaon in Solapur covers 14.50 acres and is taken on a 25-year lease. A one-time payment has been made by issuing shares worth 2.90 million rupees to the owners of the land.

The company has an agreement for technology transfer and project supervision with Flodac B.V. of Netherland. The flowers produced will be exported through Flodac to be auctioned in Holland. The marketing tie-up is for two years from the first harvest.

Land and site development for the project was to start in May 1996 to be completed by November 1996. The project is already delayed by four months and the first plucking of the flowers is scheduled for March 1997. The company has not given any financial projections.

Source/Note - Research supplied by Sebastian Dominic of Resource Base, a New Delhi-based private investment consultancy firm. Tel: 578 0840. This data is for investor information only and does not constitute a recommendation by Reuters.
